correctness.rationale: Exact affine-plane incidence identities yield an orthogonal decomposition of the zero-sum space into q parallel-class contrasts, \(q^2-1\) copies of a \(2\)-by-\(2\) coupled block, and one global contrast. The class eigenvalue switches sign at the exact logarithmic threshold. A monotonicity argument for the coupled-sector determinant proves its negativity for all permitted exponents, with a binary endpoint exception. Concavity of real powers with exponent between zero and one gives a strictly negative quadratic upper bound for the global mode. All dimensions and Gaussian equivalence follow algebraically. The checker independently passed 169 assertion groups for field orders 2,3,4,5,7, including BFS distances at q≤5; these finite tests are not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Finite affine planes and their incidence graphs are canonical test geometries for distance-powered Gaussian similarity kernels. The sharp full family classification is valid without field coordinates; it locates the exact parallel-line obstruction to Hilbert representability, detects the exceptional binary degeneracy, and gives minimal Euclidean dimensions and a sharp collapsing exponent asymptotic. These are structural all-order facts, not parameter substitutions or a small computation.
